title: Finding suitably generic points on curves with an application to the construction of rigid real closed fields
summary: Let $K$ be an algebraically closed field of characteristic 0 and transcendence degree at least 2. Let $C\subset K^2$ be an irreducible curve defined over $K$ but not defined over the algebraic closure of $\mathbb Q$. There is $(x ,y)$ a $K$-point of $C$ such that $x$ and $y$ are algebraically independent.
